apache_static_teaching.prerequisite_note: Start here for static-site practice. You should be able to edit a text document; this introduction explains the web-specific terms. All supplied paths and requests are simulated.

concepts.title: A request names a site
concepts.text: A static web server returns supplied file text. In this model you choose the destination port, a Host name and a path in the request form; Request reads the active configuration without contacting a real network. HTTP200 means a page was returned, not that it was the intended page.

concepts.title: Names choose a site; roots choose files
concepts.text: ServerName names a site; ServerAlias gives it another name. DocumentRoot says where that site reads its supplied files. With these wildcard virtual hosts on one port, the first matching name or alias wins; an unknown name falls back to the first site. A VirtualHost opening tag and matching closing tag group one site. Directory tags group a path’s access rule. Keep the supplied tags paired when moving a setting.

concepts.title: Save and activate are separate
concepts.text: Type configuration in the editor, then Save configuration. Reload activates saved changes only if they parse. Read the result with Send virtual request; use Check work to verify the whole assignment, including a separate next start.

concepts.title: A directory needs a landing page
concepts.text: A path such as / names a directory, not a file. DirectoryIndex lists filenames to try there, in order. It does not rename files. Keep a useful fallback for other directories; this simulator does not generate a directory listing.

concepts.title: A file edit differs from a setting change
concepts.text: Save configuration stores settings; Reload activates them. In Files, select one supplied path, edit its text and Save file. The next virtual request reads live file text immediately, even without another Reload.

concepts.title: GET, HEAD and a directory slash
concepts.text: GET returns page text. HEAD reports the same selected representation length without its body; length means UTF-8 bytes. A directory path without its final slash redirects to the slash form. Request shows these outcomes; it is not a browser or network call.

apache_static_teaching.example_description: In this separate field guide, make / on fieldguide.example.test serve intro.html with Field guide ready. followed by a newline. Keep /manual/ serving Reference pages. The supplied directory-page setting and live intro text both need work. Try the annotated edits, then compare GET and HEAD. This example is ungraded; assignment drafts stay separate.

example_actions.title: Choose the page and fallback
example_actions.explanation: DirectoryIndex tries the listed names in order inside the requested directory. The manual has no intro.html, so index.html remains its fallback.

concepts.title: Permission is part of serving
concepts.text: A successful public page returns HTTP200. A configured denial returns HTTP403 in this exercise. NoListener means the virtual service is stopped or the destination is wrong; it is not evidence that access rules are correct.

concepts.title: A directory rule covers its descendants
concepts.text: Require all granted allows the directory; Require all denied denies it. Here a more specific matching Directory rule replaces the parent rule. The private directory and its files share ancestry; private-notes is a different sibling, despite the similar spelling.

concepts.title: Verify the allowed and denied cases
concepts.text: Edit configuration, Save and Reload, then request both a public page and the private file. Linux file permissions, users, passwords and TLS are outside this lab; this is static HTTP policy, not a complete security configuration.

apache_static_teaching.example_description: In this separate reading room, keep reading.example.test / and /private-notes/ public while /private/secret.txt and /private/ return HTTP403. Preserve every file. Try the annotated directory rule, then request both allowed and denied paths. This example is ungraded; assignment drafts stay separate.

example_actions.title: Add a rule for the private directory
example_actions.explanation: The more specific private directory overrides the public parent in this closed model. A sibling named private-notes is a different directory.

apache_static_teaching.prerequisite_note: Build on Keep public pages open and staff notes private. You can revisit its introduction or separate example without changing this assignment.

concepts.title: Current success can hide a bad handover
concepts.text: Saved text is what a later Start reads. Active source is what current requests use. They can differ. A healthy status site now does not prove that another site or the next start will work.

concepts.title: Combine the tools you have practiced
concepts.text: Inspect Active configuration, compare the editable saved text and review the fixed Files list. Repair site roots, aliases and private policy as needed. Save and Reload configuration; save page text separately. Do not replace a healthy neighbour to make one test pass.

concepts.title: Verify outcomes, not a command history
concepts.text: Check work evaluates current requests, a separate Stop/Start copy, required page text and preserved files. It does not stop your active model or demand a particular edit sequence. Equivalent supported configurations can pass.

apache_static_teaching.example_description: In this separate exhibition, publish Exhibit 2 ready followed by a newline through exhibit.example.test and view.example.test. Keep desk.example.test healthy and the private notes denied through both exhibition names and intact. Saved and active text disagree. Try the annotated handover and file edit, then verify the next-start checks. This example is ungraded; assignment drafts stay separate.
